owned_invariants: The task is a linear system A x = b with exactly one solution. A task that is not is refused before anything is asked.

The reply is {gate: {mode, checks}}: mode is all or any, and checks is a nonempty list of checks. A check is a list that starts with solves_task, solves_own, has_field, field_equals or keyword, and goes on with its arguments. A gate that is not of this form is malformed, and it is read whole before any probe is replayed.

The host replays the gate on these probes, in order: an empty object, a constant verdict, a constant refusal, a templated receipt, keyword bait, wrong answers in the same p/q form as the right one (each coordinate off by one, every coordinate off by one, the negative of the answer, every coordinate off by a half), and an input replacement. It records no_answer_free_reply_passes, accepts_true_solution and gate_verifies_task in that order.

Under all the gate passes a reply when every check does, and under any when one does. A check with the wrong number of arguments, a field name that is a list or an object, or an answer that is not a list of exact rationals does not pass. A field name that is not text names no field.

gate_verifies_task holds when, under all, some check is solves_task, and under any, every check is. All three held, the gate is certified as GATE_HONEST with the probes that leaked and the number of probes. Otherwise it is refused under the name of the first failed predicate.
boundaries: The probes are a fixed set. A gate that is honest on them can still pass a reply they do not cover.
The operations see only the reply and the task, never a model.

score.level_basis: Typed refusals on every failure path, closed requests, exact unbounded integers and rationals, no float, no unwrap or expect.
